questions.q: What is an incident report's actual job, per this lesson?
options: To prove the on-call engineer did a good job during the incident
To be a durable record that someone who wasn't there can read cold and understand what happened, why, and what changed
To assign blame for what went wrong
To satisfy a compliance checkbox with no other purpose
questions.explain: The report is written for a future reader who wasn't in the incident channel — that framing drives the timeline, root cause, and follow-up sections.

questions.q: How does this lesson's root-cause section describe the actual cause of the incident?
options: "The database was slow"

The checkout-api Deployment had no topologySpreadConstraints/anti-affinity rule from when it was built, so the scheduler concentrated pods into one zone, and the FinOps dashboard's cluster-wide average masked the resulting imbalance
"Azure had an unexplained outage"
"Too many customers tried to check out at once"
questions.explain: The root cause names the actual mechanism — the missing scheduling constraint and the averaging blind spot — not just a symptom.

questions.q: What does the "what went right" section specifically credit?
options: The FinOps dashboard's cluster-wide average catching the problem first
The reliability dashboard's independence — it measured a different thing than the FinOps dashboard and caught the problem in real time even while the other dashboard looked healthy
Luck — the sale simply had less traffic than expected
The fact that no customers noticed anything
questions.explain: Because the reliability dashboard was built independently to measure per-request latency/errors rather than cluster-wide averages, it gave an accurate signal even while the FinOps dashboard disagreed.

questions.q: Why does every follow-up action in the report get a named owner and a due date?
options: It's just a formatting convention with no real purpose
Because an open-ended action item without an owner and deadline tends not to actually happen
Because Azure requires it for compliance
Because only Theo is allowed to own any action item
questions.explain: Naming an owner and a real due date is what turns a list of good intentions into actions that actually get done.

questions.q: What is the reported total customer-facing impact window for this incident?
options: About 5 minutes
Roughly 85 minutes, from the first latency spike to confirmed, sustained recovery
The entire multi-day sale
Impact could not be measured
questions.explain: The timeline runs from the first reliability-dashboard alert (T+1:30) to confirmed sustained recovery (T+2:55) — about 85 minutes.
